chain.label: Boeing's parts-removal BPI complex and unclear; corrective actions ineffective
chain.trigger: Boeing's BPI for performing parts removals lacked the clarity, conciseness, and ease of use necessary to be an effective tool for workers in the manufacturing process

chain.label: Unstructured on-the-job training; no personnel experienced with opening MED plugs on duty
chain.trigger: Boeing's on-the-job training for generating removal records was insufficient... no personnel experienced with opening or closing an MED plug were on duty

chain.label: FAA compliance surveillance and audit planning failed to catch systemic BPI nonconformance
chain.trigger: the FAA's ineffective compliance enforcement surveillance and audit planning activities, which failed to adequately identify and ensure that Boeing addressed the repetitive and systemic nonconformance issues

chain.label: Discrepant rivets in edge frame forward of left MED plug required rework access
chain.trigger: Boeing personnel identified workmanship discrepancies with five rivets in the edge frame forward of the left MED plug

chain.label: Left MED plug opened (four bolts removed) with no removal record generated
chain.trigger: whoever opened the left MED plug did not generate a removal record

caused_by.evidence: manufacturing personnel who encounter difficulties working through all the complexities of the BPI guidance may be more likely to erroneously conclude that a removal record is not needed

decreased the likelihood that door team personnel with limited exposure to nonroutine tasks would be able to correctly perform the process for opening an MED plug, including generating the required removal record
lacked the functionality necessary to identify repetitive and systemic discrepancies and nonconformance issues with the BPI for parts removals
To allow access for the removal and replacement of the discrepant rivets, Boeing personnel needed to open the left MED plug

chain.label: Plug closed during second shift without reinstalling bolts and attachment hardware
chain.trigger: The left MED plug was subsequently closed without its securing bolts and attachment hardware

caused_by.evidence: the absence of the documented steps for the bolts and hardware to be reinstalled
only door team personnel were allowed to perform work on doors and MED plugs, but none were on duty at the time the left MED plug was closed

chain.label: No quality assurance inspection of the plug closure performed
chain.trigger: due to the absence of a removal record indicating that the left MED plug installation had been disturbed, no quality assurance inspection of the plug closure was performed

caused_by.evidence: there was no indication of the steps needed to properly close the plug and that quality assurance signoffs were needed to verify that the left MED plug installation had been restored

chain.label: MED plug design had no secondary retention or visual indication of missing bolts
chain.trigger: a design enhancement to add two secondary retention devices to prevent an MED plug from moving upward in the event that the vertical movement arrestor bolts and upper guide track bolts were not installed

chain.label: Airplane delivered and flown with all four plug-securing bolts missing
chain.trigger: the four bolts that secured the left MED plug to prevent it from moving upward vertically were missing before the newly manufactured airplane was delivered to Alaska Airlines

caused_by.evidence: the absence of bolt contact damage or deformation around the holes... indicates that the four bolts... were missing before the plug moved upward off the stop pads
any quality assurance inspections that could have detected the left MED plug's missing hardware did not occur due to the lack of the removal record

chain.label: Plug crept upward over prior flights, disengaged stop fittings, and separated in flight
chain.trigger: the left MED plug was able to become displaced gradually upward... until, during the accident flight, it displaced upward enough to disengage from its stop fittings and separate in flight

caused_by.evidence: On a normal MED plug installation, plug vertical movement is prevented by four bolts... none of the four bolts were present
secondary retention devices... would also prevent the sidewall panels from being installed unless the devices were engaged

chain.label: Rapid cabin depressurization climbing through about 14,830 ft
chain.trigger: experienced an in-flight separation of the left mid exit door (MED) plug and rapid depressurization when climbing through about 14,830 ft

caused_by.evidence: the airplane had a hole in the fuselage where the left MED plug... had been installed

chain.label: One flight attendant and seven passengers minor injuries; substantial airplane damage
chain.trigger: One flight attendant and 7 passengers received minor injuries; ... and the airplane sustained substantial damage

caused_by.evidence: the flight deck door opened forcefully and struck her, bruising her right arm and knee

chain.label: Emergency descent and safe return landing at Portland
chain.trigger: The flight and cabin crews executed the emergency procedures in response to the rapid depressurization, and the flight returned to PDX for a safe landing

caused_by.evidence: their decision to descend the airplane and return to the departure airport was timely and appropriate
